topic: Polaris systematic excess (c6 verification of c5 H1/H2a/H2b self-applies)
our_argument_summary: WIN-065 is Refuted by Data. Three centuries of pole-star astrometry establish Polaris's ~0.66° offset from true celestial pole (epoch 2026.0); the dome's claimed +0.27° 'systematic excess' at 35.9°N is within Polaris's known diurnal-circle envelope (1σ time-averaged ≈ 0.47° RMS by 0.66°/√2). The dome's own coordinate table contradicts PRED-NEW-001: Oslo Polaris elevation 59.90° vs WGS84 59.91°N (essentially zero excess), and 22 of 24 cities match WGS84 to ±0.05°. PRED-NEW-001 registered 2026-03-12 post-dates the standard observations it 'predicts' — retrodiction, not prospective. Dome's own site lists the broader 'Polaris altitude matches latitude' prediction as FALSIFIED (2026-03-15), making simultaneous claim/refutation incoherent. n(r)-refraction structural dilemma (Section 1.8) blocks the high-latitude escape clause.

This was a class:'verification' singleton review of three c5 holes (c5 reported as H1/H2a/H2b in the queue reason; the c5 review JSON labeled them holes_found[0] = 'H0/Chapel Hill' and holes_found[1] = 'H1/subject-ambiguity' with two recipient fields). Flagging as minor in keeping with c5's grading of the same defect class.

Math sanity-check on the patched detail_evidence: the '5×–25× smaller' ratio against the '+1.4° to +5.5°' prediction range gives 1.4/0.267 = 5.24× lower bound and 5.5/0.267 = 20.6× upper bound. The c5 recommendation phrased the upper bound as '25×' which is ~20% loose against the literal arithmetic (20.6× ≈ '20×'). Decline to flag as a new hole — the c5 reviewer authored that phrasing and the decider executed the c5 recommendation verbatim; quibbling with the c5-authored rounding would be goalpost-moving and the rhetorical claim ('5× to 25× smaller — i.e., orders of magnitude smaller than predicted') is unimpeachable at the precision the dome model itself operates at. Surface in summary_for_decider as a no-action note in case a future cycle wants a precision tightening.
